item.title: Free agency the new norm? ‘They’re not doing anyone’s contract outside top 15’
item.description: Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC We could see a lot more UFC fighters hitting free agency in the future. It used to be a rarity to see a fighter fight out their contract and enter free agency. The general policy was to see fighters sign a new deal before competing in the final bout on their existing contract. Not any more, according to UFC bantamweight Elijah Smith. Smith came into the UFC through Dana White’s Contender Series and has gone 4-0 with the promotion, three of those ending via finish. He’s not one of those boring decision merchants with no highlights to his name. So it was shocking to hear he wasn’t offered a new contract before fighting out his current contract against Davey Grant last weekend in Las Vegas. And that may be the new norm. “I knew that this was my last fight of my contract, and I was always told that we would probably renew a contract right before the last fight,” Smith told Ariel Helwani. “That didn’t happen. My manager got back to me. He said it’s something that they haven’t done before and they’re not doing anybody’s contract that’s outside of the top 15.” Elijah Smith sheds light on a potential change to the UFC's contract renewal policy: “I'm gonna give it to you guys cutthroat. I'm not gonna sugarcoat anything. I'm gonna tell y'all straight up right here, right now. I knew that this was my last fight of my contract, and I was… pic.twitter.com/WsLPtMSEBt — Ariel Helwani (@arielhelwani) November 10, 2026 “I was surprised,” he continued. “Coming off two finishes, I’m young, I’m marketable, I’m an exciting fighter. Fans want to see me fight. So I was super surprised. From what I’ve heard, that’s not the case in most instances.” “So I don’t know if they want to save money or something or there’s too many people on the roster, but yeah, that’s what it was. I got the fight and they’re not redoing anybody’s contract outside the top 15. So I guess everyone’s just fighting out their contract. I don’t know if that’s for all the weight classes or just the bantamweight weight class, but that’s what was told to me.” For years the UFC has been criticized for being so aggressive when it came to keeping fighters signed to the organization. If you weren’t willing to sign a new contract, there was a good chance you’d end up on the matchmakers’ bad side, potentially affecting your ability to return. That’s no longer the case for those outside the top 15, even firecrackers like Smith. Will this be good for them, or just make things less stable for those starting out their UFC careers?

item.title: Chiefs Facing Tyreek Hill Decision After Josh Downs Trade
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs were constantly linked to Tyreek Hill ahead of the trade deadline. However, the team traded for Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts instead to bolster its receiving corps. It now faces a decision on the veteran wide receiver. Several analysts and experts considered the position as Kansas City’s “weak spot” and believed it would trade for a wideout. The Chiefs ultimately proved them right by landing Downs in exchange for a fourth- and fifth-round pick. His route running and speed will be a huge weapon for Patrick Mahomes and another target he can maximize. Hill, on the other hand, suffered a gruesome in injury in September 2025 with the Miami Dolphins. He sustained a dislocated left knee and multiple torn ligaments and immediately underwent surgery. The 32-year-old finished last season with 21 receptions for 265 yards and a touchdown. Miami released him last February and remains a free agent. item.title: Gabriel Magalhaes defends Barcelona star Raphinha over Brazil statements: ‘Many misinterpreted what he said’
item.description: Gabriel Magalhaes defends Barcelona star Raphinha over Brazil statements: ‘Many misinterpreted what he said’ Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes has publicly defended Barcelona winger Raphinha following criticism of his recent comments about managing his playing time with the Brazilian national team. Speaking at a press conference in Singapore on Wednesday, the centre-back insisted that his teammate’s words had been misunderstood and emphasised his commitment to representing Brazil. Raphinha attracted criticism after explaining that Carlo Ancelotti understood the need to manage his minutes because he was still recovering from an injury. The Barcelona forward had stressed that he was not yet fully fit and wanted the national team coach to take his physical condition into consideration. “The national team coach will know how to manage my playing time. We’ve spoken, and he knows I’m not yet at 100% fitness. “I ask Barcelona fans not to worry about this,” said Raphinha during his contract renewal ceremony. Gabriel Magalhaes insists Raphinha was misunderstood Raphinha was criticised for his statement on national team coach Carlo Ancelotti. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Gabriel, who also has experience dealing with injuries during international duty, believes the reaction to Raphinha’s comments was misplaced. The Arsenal defender explained that professional footballers cannot always maintain the same physical and mental intensity throughout a demanding calendar. “We are high-level players, and what we always want is to play. I think many misinterpreted what Raphinha said. We are human, and sometimes we need to rest, even mentally. “In Europe, we play every two or three days, and there are many matches. “When we join the national team, we want to make the most of our time here and learn, but many misinterpret some statements, and that’s what happened with Raphinha,” he explained. Brazil dressing room backs Barcelona winger Gabriel Magalhaes has defended Raphinha. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) Gabriel also made it clear that Raphinha’s comments had not created any concern within the Brazilian dressing room. Instead, he highlighted the Barcelona forward’s dedication and importance to the national team. “Within the group, we didn’t understand his words to mean that he came here to rest or anything like that. “We know his dedication to the national team well; his commitment is exemplary, and he is an ideal player for us.” The discussion comes as Brazil prepare for two friendlies in Singapore , facing Japan on November 14 before meeting the hosts three days later. Source: Mundo Deportivo

item.title: "I might have deserved the opportunity a little more" – Ter Stegen opens up on rivalry with Neuer
item.description: "I might have deserved the opportunity a little more" – Ter Stegen opens up on rivalry with Neuer Heading into Germany's upcoming games against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen has been named as Jürgen Klopp undisputed first choice in goal. For the 34-year-old, this marks a welcome change after years of playing second fiddle to Manuel Neuer and struggling with injuries. In an interview with Sport Bild, ter Stegen looks back on his long-standing rivalry with the now 40-year-old Bayern Munich shot-stopper, who announced his international retirement for good after last summer's World Cup. While ter Stegen clearly has huge respect for Neuer's qualities, he makes no secret of the fact that he would have liked to play more than the 45 games he has featured in for Germany at senior level. “Manuel Neuer is not simply a great goalkeeper. We don't need to fool ourselves about that: he is probably one of the best goalkeepers of all time. He also had an enormous standing within the national team, and rightly so. However, he was also held back by injuries,” ter Stegen said. “And who knows more about that than I do, unfortunately? Nevertheless, I believe a certain level of competition pushes the goalkeeper who gets to play to improve. That's how it was with us. “Even so, the question naturally remains: would I rather have been playing? Of course! But the coaches we had with the national team chose Manu. You have to respect that, and I have to accept it. That's simply part of sport.” The 34-year-old did admit that there were times when he felt he deserved to play ahead of Neuer, despite not being given the opportunity. “Did I sometimes have to bite my tongue? Did I sometimes swear under my breath when nobody was listening? Certainly! There were also moments when I felt I might have deserved the opportunity a little more,” he said. One particularly bitter moment for ter Stegen came at the 2018 World Cup, when Neuer managed to return from a long-term injury and reclaim his place in the starting line-up ahead of him despite lacking match practice. “That was the most bitter moment, but I don't want to revisit it. The fact remains that the coach (Jogi Löw at the time, ed.) makes the decision. You can get as angry as you like,” said ter Stegen, who is currently Ajax's first-choice goalkeeper while on loan from FC Barcelona.

item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Chad Tracy finishes third in AL Manager of the Year race
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Manager Chad Tracy #17 of the Boston Red Sox looks on from the dugout prior to the game between the Chicago Cubs and the Boston Red Sox at Tropicana Field on Sunday, September 27, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Scott Audette/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Is Manager of the Year the dumbest award in baseball? I think it is. For starters, no one cares about it. I mean no one. Can you name a single winner of the Manager of the Year Award of the past 10 years? Don’t even think about lying to me, you obviously cannot. And that’s a good thing. Baseball is a player’s game. This isn’t college hoops, where the ego-puffing men performatively screaming on the sideline are bigger stars than the players themselves. Baseball managers aren’t stars at all. They’re just kind of there. To belabor the sky metaphor, baseball managers are clouds, at best. And because baseball is a player’s game — one that’s decided on the field instead of in the pages of a playbook — almost no one on the outside is even capable of evaluating the job a manager does. Managers don’t have elaborate styles of play they bring from one team to another. They don’t spend days designing defensive schemes that befuddle more talented teams. Their job is mostly to keep the clubhouse happy and pull a pitcher at the right moment. That’s just about it. And because the job is so hard to evaluate from the outside, voting usually follows a predictable pattern: voters just give it to the manager of the team that had a better season than anyone expected. They do this despite the fact that we all know that, every single season, there will be flukey teams who get a little magic fairy dust sprinkled on them and make a surprising playoff run. That’s just how baseball works and, more often than not, those teams go right on back to being mediocre-to-bad the next season. So, e.g., we give the 2023 NL Manager of the Year to Skip Schumaker. After all, the 2022 Marlins only won 69 games, so Schumaker guiding the same team to 84 wins the next season obviously means he did an amazing job, right? Of course — just please try to ignore the fact that he must have forgotten how to manage the next year, because the same team with the same manager subsequently went 62-100 the very next season. All of this is to say: I don’t really care that Chad Tracy didn’t win the American League Manager of the Year last night. He finished third, behind winner Will Venable of the White Sox and runner-up Kevin Cash of the Rays. Did either Venable or Cash truly do a better job than Tracy? No one knows. item.title: Joe Lacob talks Juste Jocyte’s future after Natalie Nakase drama
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Golden State Valkyries owner Joe Lacob isn’t shutting the door on Juste Jocyte. Juste Jocyte didn’t bite her tongue after spending basically the entire WNBA Finals glued to the pine, seeing just six total minutes on the floor. The 20-year-old made her feelings known in an interview with the Lithuanian media, making it clear she was miserable with how Natalie Nakase used her. Now, heading into the offseason, Jocyte is putting the Valkyries front office on notice, telling them she has zero interest in riding the bench next year, and she won’t stick around without real minutes. Joe Lacob issues an update on Juste Jocyte’s future Joe Lacob is trying to play damage control before the situation spirals. Instead of taking the bait and firing back at Jocyte’s comments, the Valkyries owner is playing the long game, making it clear he doesn’t want to let the 20-year-old walk away. He said: “I kind of understand she’s competitive and would like to win and didn’t play. But she’s also only 20. We had a pretty great roster, very deep. I think she can be a very good player and we’d really love to have her back. “So I think she will certainly earn a lot more playing time in the future. She didn’t get to play as much as she wanted to, and that’s understandable. “I think she can be a very good player and we would really love to have her back.” Even with Lacob trying to play nice, it’s hard to picture Jocyte sticking around in the Bay. That bridge with Nakase is burned, and Golden State isn’t about to let locker room bad blood poison the culture they’re building. Once trust is shot, a clean break is the only realistic way out. item.title: No. 1 junior Asterisk Talley not signing with Stanford but remains committed
item.description: The top-ranked female golfer in the Class of 2027 won’t be signing during the week-long early signing period, which began Wednesday. While Stanford will sign another highly ranked recruit in Anna Fang, the Cardinal will hold off in adding No. 1 junior Asterisk Talley, the reigning U.S. Women’s Amateur champion who is ranked fourth in the World Amateur Golf Ranking. The 17-year-old Talley, who hails from Chowchilla, California, remains verbally committed to Stanford and can sign at any point, but Talley is also undecided about her future as she chases an LPGA card through the tour’s Elite Amateur Pathway. “It’s still definitely in conversation,” Talley said of playing college golf. “It’s definitely an undecided still, but I think it’s something to think about over the next few months, and it’s definitely going to be an interesting path to kind of take. Both have their upsides and their cons, too. It’s definitely going to be a go-with-the-flow kind of thing and see what happens in these coming months.” Due to NCAA rules, Stanford head coach Anne Walker cannot comment on prospective student-athletes like Talley, though she'll soon officially welcome Fang, Golf Channel’s No. 2 junior in the class behind only Wake Forest signee Amelie Zalsman, to her program. Signing Day: Ranking top classes, players for Class of 2027 Most years, the No. 1 recruit in NCAA men’s golf is up for discussion. This year, there is no debate as Miles Russell, arguably the best prospect in over a decade, signs with Florida State. Brentley Romine , Brentley Romine , Talley isn’t the first No. 1 women’s recruit not to sign during the early signing period; Yuka Saso was verbally committed to Georgia for the Class of 2020, but she never put pen to paper for the Bulldogs, instead turning professional later that November. While the launch of Talley's pro career isn't expected to be as imminent, she currently sits at 15 LEAP points and has plenty of opportunities to get to 20 and earn LPGA status. She is already exempt into four major championships next year, starting with the Chevron Championship in April. Made cuts in majors award one point while top-25s come with as additional point. item.title: MCC to introduce Spirit of Cricket Award at ILT20 Season 5
item.description: The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) will introduce a Spirit of Cricket Award at the ILT20 Season 5, recognising a team or individual who best reflects the game's values during the tournament, which begins in the UAE on November 21. The award will be presented at the end of the competition on December 20, marking the first such recognition at the six-team T20 league. MCC, the guardian of cricket's Laws, will work with the tournament organisers to promote sportsmanship and fair play among players. The partnership is part of MCC's wider effort to promote the Spirit of Cricket across the game. The Club has previously worked with ICC Europe to present similar awards at three men's sub-regional World Cup qualification events earlier this year. Rob Lynch, MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations, said franchise leagues could play an important role in setting standards for player behaviour. “MCC sees franchise leagues as the standard-bearers for playing the game in the right way – playing hard but playing fair and with a smile on your face,” Lynch said. He added that the competitive nature of franchise cricket, where international team-mates often face each other, could help improve conduct across the sport. Mike Fordham, Interim Chief Operating Officer of the ILT20, said the partnership aligned with the league's emphasis on sporting values. He also pointed to the participation of players from 19 cricketing nations across its six franchises this season. “The tournament has always been hugely competitive with top quality cricket on display. Our matches have always been played in the right spirit with cricket’s traditional sporting values remaining at the forefront,” Fordham said. Season 5 will run from November 21 to December 20, with matches scheduled at the Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi, Dubai International Stadium and Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Defending champions Desert Vipers will be joined by Gulf Giants, MI Emirates, Dubai Capitals, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders and Sharjah Warriorz in the 34-match competition. Previous winners include Gulf Giants, MI Emirates and Dubai Capitals. The new recognition will be separate from the main MCC Spirit of Cricket Award, established by MCC and the BBC in 2013 in honour of Christopher Martin-Jenkins.

item.description: It was noon Friday, and the Blackhawks Ice Center just west of downtown Chicago was teeming with teenage hockey players and their equipment. Three of the center’s four ice surfaces were in use for a weekend hockey tournament. The fourth rink, where Jason Brown was headed, would be filled with 16 figure skaters of various ages and skill levels, from the abilities that have made the 31-year-old Brown a two-time Olympian to those of tiny 8-year-olds trying to master a waltz jump. Brown folded up the workout mat he had squeezed into one unoccupied space in a lobby behind one of the rinks. He put the devices used to stretch and warm up back into a small roller suitcase, laced his skates and walked over to the fourth rink, where an open freestyle session was beginning. 2026 Saatva Skate America: How to watch, schedule, preview of figure skating Grand Prix Skate America, the biggest annual international figure skating event in the U.S., airs live on NBC Sports and Peacock. item.title: Drew Rosenhaus shares what he thinks will happen if San Francisco 49ers release Brandon Aiyuk
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Brandon Aiyuk officially made his return to the San Francisco 49ers last Friday, and his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, believes the player could either return to the team or be moved as a free agent. The wide receiver was at loggerheads with the franchise and called out coach Kyle Shanahan and members of the front office. However, after approaching the league, he was reinstated, and this means the 49ers now have two weeks to decide what they want to do with him. Aiyuk last played for the 49ers in October 2024 and has since been out due to an injury. After being reinstated, he has passed his physical examination, but the 49ers have already made the decision to move on from him. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, is confident that won’t change Aiyuk’s plans for the rest of the season. “Brandon will either play for the 49ers when the two weeks are up, or they can decide to release him, in which case he will be a free agent. And I expect that there will be interest in him. I definitely expect him to play this season. Judging by the comments from coach Shanahan, it doesn’t sound like they plan on bringing Brandon back. So, when the two weeks are over, it’s my job to potentially find a new team for him. And I’m confident now that he’s healthy, he will play,” said Rosenhaus on The Pat McAfee Show. All offseason, Aiyuk was pushing for a move to the Washington Commanders to team up with Jayden Daniels, who was his teammate at Arizona State University. However, things got a little complicated when Aiyuk then called out Daniels, leading to the QB even unfollowing the 49ers player. Before his injury, Aiyuk was one of the best WRs in the league and even made the Second Team All-Pro. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers have the NBA’s best record at 10-2, and new arrival Walker Kessler has played his part in their early success. Kessler has impressed on defense, and former Laker Robert Horry likes what he has seen from the big man on that end of the floor. What Horry, who won three titles with the Lakers, doesn’t like, though, is Kessler’s offensive game, and he urged him to improve on the Big Shot Bob Podcast . “You know what’s really scary about Walker Kessler?” Horry said. “Hey, I know guys in elementary got better post moves than him. He got no post moves, man. I’m like, who is teaching this dude any post moves? You’re seven f***ing feet tall. Get you a little jump hook, man. You don’t have to dunk everything.” Kessler really doesn’t have a reliable post move. The 25-year-old is primarily a rim-runner, and if you are good at that next to Luka Doncic , you’ll score some points. Kessler is averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 2.3 blocks per game for the Lakers in 2026-27. Over 60 percent of his field goal attempts have been within three feet of the basket, and only 1.8 percent have come from beyond 10 feet. Now, Kessler showed off some range in the 2025-26 season for the Utah Jazz . He went 6-8 from three in five games before needing season-ending shoulder surgery. So, when the Lakers acquired Kessler, the No. 22 pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, from the Jazz in the summer, the expectation was that he’d be a threat from beyond the arc. He even shared that head coach JJ Redick wanted him to shoot more threes , but he hasn’t even attempted a single one through 12 games. “I don’t even think he wants to score ’cause I’ve seen him get offensive rebounds and kick that b***h out instead of crunching that b***h,” Horry said. “… I’m like, dude, you 7 ft tall. Get you a power dribble. Go up and dunk that b***h too. Like [Shaquille O’Neal], you monkey dunk that b***h. That’s what he said. That’s what Shaq used to say. Now, teams like the player who gets the offensive rebound to kick it out for an open three. That could well be the case here, but we don’t know for sure. While Kessler isn’t the perfect offensive center, that wasn’t why the Lakers gave him a four-year, $130 million contract and gave up two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to the Jazz. item.description: Manager praises new Arsenal loanee after debut Arsenal youngster Khari Ranson began a short-term loan move to Billericay Town on Tuesday night, and he’s already made his debut for the club. Photo via Ranson on Instagram Arsenal confirmed on Tuesday that 19-year-old goalkeeper Khari Ranson has joined National League South side Billericay Town on an initial 28-day loan. The teenager was straight into the action with his new side later that night, making the starting lineup for an Essex Senior Cup match against Little Oakley FC . The debut couldn’t have gone much better, with Ranson keeping a clean sheet as his new team won 7-0 to reach the quarter-finals. Photo via Ranson on Instagram Manager Danny Scopes was pleased, telling the media that “Khari in goal did well”. But there will be tougher tests to come than eighth-tier side Little Oakley over the course of the next four weeks. The schedule is helping to ease Ranson in, as Billericay’s next fixture is another cup game against lower-league opponents. On Saturday, Billericay will face another eighth-tier side in Waltham Abbey in the FA Trophy. After that, Billericay will return to their National League South campaign, the sixth tier of English football. Their next league game is against high-flying Truro City , and Ranson is likely to be tested a lot more in that game. Photo via Ranson on Instagram Ranson had made seven appearances for the Arsenal u21s this season, prior to his loan move. This loan spell is offering him his first taste of senior football, and it’s not impossible the two clubs could look to extend it when it ends next month. Photo via Ranson on Instagram

item.title: Tributes pour in for longtime Iona basketball announcer Gary Stanley
item.description: Credit: Iona Athletic Gary Stanley, the voice of the Iona Gaels men’s basketball team for over three decades, has passed away at 73. The Iona men’s basketball account shared the news on social media. “Iona Athletics mourns the passing of Gary Stanley, a longtime voice of Iona and Gaels men’s basketball,” read the post. “Gary’s passion for Iona and memorable presence behind the microphone made him an important part of the Gael family. His contributions will not be forgotten. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with Gary’s family, friends, and all who had the privilege of knowing him.” Iona Athletics mourns the passing of Gary Stanley, a longtime voice of Iona and Gaels men’s basketball. Gary’s passion for Iona and memorable presence behind the microphone made him an important part of the Gael family. His contributions will not be forgotten. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with Gary’s family, friends and all who had the privilege of knowing him. Rest in peace, Gary. — Iona Men’s Basketball (@IonaGaelsMBB) November 9, 2026 Starting in 1985, Stanley served for over three decades as the radio play-by-play announcer for Iona, calling games for WVOX and 93.5 WRTN, most notably alongside analyst Ed Ingles. After Ingles retired, Stanley continued calling Iona games alongside rotating analysts such as Bill Daughtry, Vin Parise, and Kevin Hamilton. Stanley was also a longtime sportscaster and anchor on WCBS 880 AM in New York. He worked directly for the all-news station for four years before moving to Shadow Traffic (later Clear Channel’s Total Traffic), and remained one of WCBS’s lead sports voices until 2013. His son, Casey Stanley , spent two stints as an assistant coach at Iona, including some time under Rick Pitino, and is currently the head coach of the Division II Westminster Griffins. He also shared a message about his father’s passing on social media. https://t.co/NHgNboWM9Y — Casey Stanley (@CoachStanleyWU) November 10, 2026 As news of his passing spread on social media, many of Stanley’s co-workers and peers in the sports media world offered tributes. @IonaGaelsMBB So sad to hear. Gary loved Iona and we met during a couple of NCAA @MarchMadnessMBB runs years ago. RIP Gary — Tim Brando (@TimBrando) November 10, 2026 I truly believe Gary could have done PxP anywhere. He was that good. It was a treat visiting with him and Ed Ingles before Manhattan/Iona games. Gary was tough – but earning his respect meant a great deal. I’ll miss him. — Ed Cohen (@edcohensports) November 10, 2026 Oh God, this is awful. Many a night was spent with Gary before an Iona game lamenting the Rangers’ struggles over the years. He and the late great Ed Ingles were two of the first friends I made covering the MAAC. My condolences to his son, @CoachStanleyWU, and his family. RIP. — Jaden Daly (@DalyDoseOfHoops) November 9, 2026 The post Tributes pour in for longtime Iona basketball announcer Gary Stanley, dead at 73 appeared first on Awful Announcing .
